Here's the decision from the design review for LEDGERLIB-107: the sequence restarts every calendar year — when `last_number` belongs to an earlier year than `year`, the next number is CN-<year>-0001 (e.g. after "CN-2024-0173" the first credit note of 2025 is "CN-2025-0001"). For prorate I'm running the acceptance checks now and will flag anything ambiguous.

Hi! The cross-rate decision is in my handover notes: convert between two non-base currencies in a single step, cents * rate[target] / rate[source], and round once at the end. Don't round-trip through the base currency — the double rounding can drift by a cent. Hope that helps with LEDGERLIB-112! 🙌
Hi! I just implemented allocate_cents (LEDGERLIB-104) this cycle. It should be working now - let me know if the acceptance tests still fail on your side.

On ordering: the design review decision I noted was 'same-day due dates settle smallest open amount first, ties keep input order' - that's specifically about invoices falling due on the SAME day. It doesn't contradict 'oldest due date first' as the primary sort. So primary key = due date ascending, then for same due date -> smallest open amount, then input order. Hope that helps!
